title: Biopsychology: neurons and the brain
note: Neurons signal electrically within the cell and chemically between cells. An action potential runs down the axon; at the synapse, neurotransmitters cross the gap and bind to receptors. Brain regions specialize, but most behavior depends on many regions working together.

read.title: How one neuron talks to the next
text: A neuron at rest holds a small negative charge inside, about -70 millivolts. Signals arriving at its dendrites nudge that charge up or down. If the charge at the start of the axon reaches threshold, about -55 millivolts, the neuron fires an action potential: a brief spike that races down the axon.

Firing is all-or-none. A stronger stimulus does not make a bigger spike; instead, it makes the neuron fire more often. Myelin, a fatty wrapping made by glial cells, speeds the trip, because the signal jumps between the gaps in the myelin called nodes of Ranvier.

At the end of the axon, the terminal buttons release neurotransmitters into the synaptic cleft. These chemicals bind to receptors on the next neuron like a key in a lock, making that neuron more or less likely to fire. Glutamate usually excites; GABA usually inhibits.

The signal must then be cleared. Leftover neurotransmitter is pumped back into the sending neuron, a process called reuptake. Many drugs work at this step, or by mimicking a neurotransmitter (agonists) or blocking its receptor (antagonists).
